title: Postmortem: regional affinity oscillation caused repeated SLO misses for embeddings.generate
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: During a 2.5 hour window on 2026-03-10 we observed repeated 99th percentile latency and increased error rate on the embeddings.generate endpoint for customers routed through EU and US regions. The pattern was oscillatory: traffic shifted between regions multiple times causing repeated SLO misses, elevated tail latency, and a small but visible increase in 5xx errors. This postmortem documents the timeline, root causes, mitigations taken during the incident, and concrete follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At ~09:12 UTC automated regional weight adjustments triggered by the traffic router combined with an aggressive circuit-breaker hysteresis change deployed two days earlier caused repeated traffic shifts between us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Each shift invalidated local KV caches and triggered cold GPU cache paths, producing a spike in tail latency and transient error rates that breached our 99p latency SLO for embeddings.generate for ~2.5 hours total (09:12-11:42 UTC).
impact_metrics: SLO: embeddings.generate 99p latency target 600ms — observed peak 2.1s
Error rate: 5xx spiked from baseline 0.02% to 0.9% during spikes
Affected customers: ~47 customers had >10% of requests routed through affected regions during the window
Duration: intermittent bursts across 09:12-11:42 UTC (total ~2.5h of degraded SLO)
timeline: 2026-03-10 08:55 UTC - Health monitors showed rising CPU/GPU utilization in eu-west-1 but below autoscale threshold
2026-03-10 09:08 UTC - Control-plane started applying small iterative DNS weight changes to shift 10% of traffic off eu-west-1 based on an automated routing policy
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - First observable latency spike on embeddings.generate (99p -> 1.6s); circuit-breaker in us-east-1 briefly opened on higher error rate
2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Router applies additional weight change; traffic flips back to eu-west-1 to chase lower cost profile
2026-03-10 09:20-10:30 UTC - Cycle of traffic shifts continues; each shift causes KV cache misses, longer model cold-start tails, and local autoscale churn
2026-03-10 10:35 UTC - Oncall manually pins traffic at 65/35 split and increases node warmup concurrency; tail latency temporarily improves
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Deployed temporary rollback of circuit-breaker hysteresis changes (rollback PR #GH-4812); routing weight adjustments rate-limited
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - Additional cache warmup (preload keyspaces) and disablement of cross-region DNS rebalances; latency returns to baseline
2026-03-10 11:42 UTC - Incident declared resolved, monitoring shifted to post-incident validation
root_causes: Circuit-breaker hysteresis change (deployed 2026-03-08) reduced 'hold' time and increased sensitivity to transient errors, causing faster tripping and reset cycles across regions
Routing control-plane applied small, frequent DNS weight updates with low TTL; combined with the circuit-breaker behavior this produced rapid traffic oscillation between regions
Asymmetric load-shedding thresholds between regions caused one region to shed requests earlier and then rejoin traffic rapidly, amplifying oscillation
Embeddings service relies on large on-GPU KV caches; repeated region flips invalidated warm caches causing GPU cold paths and higher latency per request
mitigations_taken: Pinned routing split to stable 65/35 while investigating (manual override)
Rollback of circuit-breaker hysteresis change (PR #GH-4812) reverted to previous hold windows
Rate-limited routing weight changes and increased DNS TTL for regional weight updates
Triggered targeted cache warmup for embeddings model keyspaces in secondary region to reduce cold-cache penalty
Notified affected customers via status page and CS team—apologized and offered post-incident summary
follow_up_actions: ENG-100128: Implement coordinated circuit-breaker state propagation (control-plane -> region routers) to avoid independent flip-flop (owner: Luca Moreno, due: 2026-04-07)
ENG-100129: Add sticky affinity for active KV cache windows so in-flight sessions remain on warmed hosts during planned rebalances (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-04-14)
ENG-100130: Introduce rate limits and smoothing for routing weight adjustments; expose metrics for weight-change frequency (owner: Network Team, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-100131: Align load-shedding thresholds across regions and add symmetric hysteresis defaults (owner: Reliability Team, due: 2026-03-31)
ENG-100132: Add synthetic canary probing for cross-region oscillation that alerts at first sign of >3 flips in 10 minutes (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-100133: Update runbook with step-by-step actions for 'regional oscillation' including how to pin traffic and force cache warmup (owner: Oncall SRE, due: 2026-03-18)
owners_and_commitments: Luca Moreno: lead implementation of coordinated circuit-breaker propagation; weekly update in project channel
Priya Shah: implement sticky KV affinity and test against synthetic traffic
Observability team: deliver new synthetic probe and dashboard, add alert run conditions
Network Team: enforce rate-limiting in routing controller and increase default DNS TTL for weight updates
post_incident_validation: 24h synthetic traffic run after mitigations showed no flips and 99p latency within SLO
Two-week retrospective monitoring scheduled to ensure no reintroduction during traffic growth
Load tests with controlled region flips executed in staging to validate sticky affinity and cache warmup effectiveness
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Weiss): confirm postmortem scope includes customer-facing remediation and check CS comms templates
Design (Mina Park): suggested a brief summary card for status page rather than raw technical detail
Security (Rui Chen): flagged that DNS TTL changes should be reviewed for compliance in private deployments
lessons_learned: Small, frequent automated routing changes are safe when backend state is fully symmetric and caches are warm. When stateful GPU caches and asymmetric shedding policies exist, routing must be conservative: rate-limited, coordinated with circuit-breaker behavior, and validated with synthetic flipping tests before enabling in production.
next_steps_notes: Owners assigned to follow-up tickets. Observability to add a dashboard tile that correlates routing weight changes, circuit-breaker state, and cache hit ratio so future oscillation can be diagnosed in <5 minutes.
communication: Customer outreach: CS ticket batch sent 2026-03-11 summarizing impact and mitigations
